newsitem.title: ESTONIA: FINAL TALKS TO SELL PART OF ESTONIAN ENERGY UNDERWAY.
newsitem.headline: FINAL TALKS TO SELL PART OF ESTONIAN ENERGY UNDERWAY.

text.p: Final negotiations are underway for the state to sell part of Estonian Energy to U.S. company Northern Power Co with an agreement expected by July, Estonia's Privatisation Agency said on Thursday.

The agency's director general Vaino Sarnet said the two parties were in final talks to agree on a business plan for a joint venture on Estonia's two main power stations at Narva in the country's northeast.
The plan, giving 50/50 ownership of the power stations that produce 95 percent of Estonia's electricity, will then go before the government for approval.
Sarnet said it included a US$250 million investment over a five year period.
"There is no certainty that this plan will be approved," Sarnet told Reuters in an interview.
"But if this business plan is approved then contracts will be drawn up."
Sarnet said the two power stations were currently only running at about 40 percent capacity so there was room to boost output and export to Lithuania, Latvia and Russia.
"But to lift production the stations must meet certain economic and environmental requirements," Sarnet said.
"This is where the investment comes in."
Sarnet said another U.S. company, Duke Power Co , had expressed an interest in Estonia's other powers stations and distribution networks.
"We have not had any formal negotiations but we have met a few times," Sarnet said.
The partial sale of Estonian Energy is part of the government's programme to privatise the country's infrastructure companies.

Under an ongoing privatisation plan, the agency expects to have sold most of the state's holdings in industrial companies by the end of 1997 to then focus on selling infrastructure companies and land.
